html:
A mass emigration of about 125,000 Cubans by boat from the harbour of Mariel in Cuba to Florida, between April and October 1980.

Cuba's economy was in trouble. In April 1980 a group of Cubans drove a bus into the Peruvian embassy in Havana seeking asylum, and when Fidel Castro withdrew the guards, over 10,000 people crowded onto its grounds. Castro then announced that anyone who wanted to leave could go from Mariel. Cuban Americans in Florida sailed over in hundreds of small boats to fetch relatives. Cuban officials also put on board people from prisons and mental hospitals.

The arrivals, called Marielitos, were mostly ordinary workers, but the prisoners got the headlines and the group faced prejudice. Many were held in camps; riots broke out at Fort Chaffee in Arkansas. Over time most settled in Miami and changed the city. The crisis embarrassed President Jimmy Carter. It was one of several waves of exile since the Cuban Revolution.
sum: A mass emigration of about 125,000 Cubans by boat from the harbour of Mariel in Cuba to Florida, between April and October 1980.
